name: Darkseid
summary: Jack Kirby's god of tyranny, who wants the universe to stop thinking. Darkseid rules the hellish planet Apokolips and hunts the Anti-Life Equation to control every mind.
origin: Darkseid is Jack Kirby's idea of pure tyranny carved in stone, and he still looms over every big DC crossover. He first peeked out in Superman's Pal Jimmy Olsen #134 in 1970, part of Kirby's Fourth World saga, then made his full entrance in Forever People #1. Born Uxas, he is one of the New Gods and the absolute ruler of Apokolips, a hellish factory planet. His great goal is the Anti-Life Equation, a formula that would wipe out free will and hope and give him control over every mind in existence. He fires Omega Beams from his eyes, is practically immortal and nearly unbreakable, and plans with cold patience. Plenty of villains want to rule the universe; Darkseid wants it to stop thinking.
powers: Omega Beams that chase their target

storyline.title: Kirby's tyrant
storyline.beat: Jack Kirby moves to DC and launches his Fourth World saga, with Darkseid as the ruler of the hellish planet Apokolips, searching for a formula to control all minds.

storyline.title: Traded sons
storyline.beat: Darkseid and Highfather of New Genesis exchange sons to seal a truce. Orion is raised on New Genesis and Scott Free on Apokolips.

storyline.title: Legion's nightmare
storyline.beat: In the Legion of Super-Heroes' Great Darkness Saga, a mysterious villain menacing the 30th century turns out to be Darkseid.

storyline.title: God falls
storyline.beat: Grant Morrison has Darkseid fall through creation into a human body and almost conquer Earth. Batman shoots him with a special bullet.

storyline.title: Why the League formed
storyline.beat: Darkseid's invasion of Earth brings together the first heroes of the new Justice League.

storyline.title: Death of a god
storyline.beat: The Anti-Monitor kills Darkseid, sending his godly power out to members of the Justice League.

gossip.text: When Kirby drew Superman for Jimmy Olsen, DC had other artists redraw his Superman faces to match the house style.
Jim Starlin's Thanos for Marvel took inspiration from Darkseid.
His Omega Beams fire from his eyes and can bend around obstacles to find their target.
He hunts for the Anti-Life Equation, which would let him control every mind.
He first appeared in Superman's Pal Jimmy Olsen, not in a Superman title.

quiz.q: Which of Darkseid's sons was raised on New Genesis?

theme.tagline: Tyrant of a fire planet with very glowing eyes.

timeline.title: Shadow over Jimmy Olsen
timeline.note: Jack Kirby slips Darkseid into Superman's Pal Jimmy Olsen #134, a teaser for his Fourth World saga.

timeline.title: The Fourth World
timeline.note: Kirby's New Gods books reveal Darkseid as the tyrant of Apokolips, hunting the Anti-Life Equation.

timeline.title: Super Powers debut
timeline.note: Darkseid makes his animated debut in Super Friends: The Legendary Super Powers Show.

timeline.title: Legends
timeline.note: Darkseid masterminds Legends, the first big crossover of the post-Crisis DC universe.

timeline.title: Final Crisis
timeline.note: Grant Morrison's Final Crisis has a fallen Darkseid nearly drag all of reality down with him.

timeline.title: The Darkseid War
timeline.note: His clash with the Anti-Monitor ends with Darkseid dead, at least for a while.

timeline.title: The Snyder Cut
timeline.note: Darkseid finally appears in a live-action movie in Zack Snyder's Justice League.
